01

THE GROWL IS THE
FORMANT MOVING.

Not the cutoff sweeping. A twelve-type zero-delay filter bank with a vowel space you can drive at audio rate, so the movement reads as a voice rather than as a filter.

  • TWO WAVETABLE / GRAINTABLE OSCILLATORS
  • SIXTEEN-VOICE UNISON, PER-VOICE DETUNE
  • 2× AND 4× OVERSAMPLING ON THE VOICE SECTION
  • −65.6 dBc ALIASING, MEASURED

02

DRAW THE RHYTHM,
NOT THE RATE.

Four LFOs with drawable curves on a triplet grid. The rate says how long a cycle lasts; what happens inside it is the shape you draw, and that is where the genre lives — growls, croaks, wobbles and sub weight, 160 of them in the box.

  • 160 FACTORY PRESETS
  • MORPH BETWEEN ANY TWO
  • RANDOMISE THAT STAYS MUSICAL
  • MODULATION IN 32-SAMPLE CHUNKS

03

FOURTEEN EFFECTS.
ANY ORDER.

Order matters and the rack respects it. Two distortions with an EQ between them sound different from the same two with an EQ after — because the EQ changes what the second curve is given.

  • OTT, DISTORTION ×2, EQ ×2, FILTER ×2
  • CHORUS, FLANGER, PHASER, HYPER
  • DIMENSION, DELAY, REVERB, LIMITER
  • 2× OVERSAMPLED WHEN ANYTHING NONLINEAR IS ON

WHERE DO I PUT THE PLUGIN?

Anywhere you like on Windows. Unzip into Downloads, double-click GNARL.exe to hear it with no DAW at all, and leave GNARL.vst3 in the same folder — then add that folder to FL Studio’s plugin search paths, or turn on Ableton’s VST3 custom folder, and rescan. macOS fixes the paths: ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/ and …/Components/ for the AU.

THE PLUGIN WINDOW IS BLANK.

The machine is missing the WebView2 runtime. The interface is a web view; without it there is nothing to draw with. It ships with Windows 11 and recent 10, and is a free download from Microsoft otherwise.

WILL IT RUN IN FL STUDIO?

It is a VST3 and is built for exactly those two. Every build is loaded the way a DAW’s scanner loads it and checked for identical sound before it ships. A real FL Studio and Ableton session is the beta’s job — tell us what you find.

HOW MUCH CPU?

Oversampling is the dial that matters: the voices run at 1×, 2×, 4× or 8×, and 2× is the default. Unison is the other: seven voices per oscillator cost seven times one. Even the phone version, in a browser, plays a heavy patch — two unison oscillators and every effect — about four times faster than real time on one server core.
